title: Short Stuff: Scratching
summary: Short Stuff episode on record scratching, companion to the full-length Vinyl records episode. Josh and Chuck trace the origins of turntablism: Theodore Livingstone (DJ Grand Wizard Theodore) accidentally scratching a record in 1975 in the Bronx when his mom told him to turn down the volume, and the hosts distinguish scratching from cutting and breakbeat DJing. They describe techniques such as the transformer scratch and the crab scratch, credit DJ Cool Herc, Grandmaster Flash and Afrika Bambaataa as early forefathers, and explain how Herbie Hancock's "Rocket" performance at the 26th Grammy Awards, with a scratch solo by Grand Mixer DXT, brought scratching into the mainstream. A brief mention of YouTube tutorials (Scratch School, Scratch Bastard, DJ Babu) is included. The episode ends with a sponsor break and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening and scope
segments.summary: Josh introduces the short stuff as a companion to the full-length vinyl records episode and notes that record scratching is hard to describe and too large for a short episode, so they focus on early history.

segments.title: Theodore's accidental scratch in 1975
segments.summary: In 1975 in the Bronx, DJ Grand Wizard Theodore accidentally scratched a record while turning down the volume after his mom told him to lower it. He realized it sounded cool and began doing it at parties and clubs.

segments.title: Scratching, cutting, and breakbeats
segments.summary: The hosts define the two basic turntablism categories: scratching, credited to Grand Wizard Theodore, and cutting, credited to DJ Cool Herc. They explain cutting with the crossfader and breakbeat technique using two copies of the same record, and connect these to juggling beats and turntablism.

segments.title: Breakbeat explanation and ad lead-in
segments.summary: The hosts explain how breakbeat lets a DJ extend a drum break indefinitely by alternating between two decks, then the episode breaks for an ad.

segments.title: Learning scratching from online tutorials
segments.summary: The hosts discuss online video tutorials (Scratch School, Scratch Bastard, DJ Babu) that demonstrate scratching, praising how instructors show mistakes and recovery. They describe the physical coordination required.

segments.title: Transformer and crab scratches
segments.summary: The hosts describe the transformer scratch, which Jazzy Jeff helped pioneer, and the crab scratch, performed by flicking the crossfader with alternating fingers. They comment on how coordinated the technique is.

segments.title: Herbie Hancock's Rocket and the Grammys
segments.summary: The hosts describe how Herbie Hancock's Rocket, performed at the 26th Grammy Awards with a scratch solo by Grand Mixer DXT, brought scratching into the mainstream. They discuss how it changed the public view of turntables beyond DJing and its influence on kids. They mention Michael Jackson and Emmanuel Lewis at the same ceremony.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing remarks and sign-off, with a note that Stuff You Should Know is produced by iHeartRadio.
